query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small boron addition (≈0.5 at.% B) to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will segregate to grain boundaries, refine the grain size, and form thin, coherent boride films that arrest micro-crack initiation and propagation. This will at least double the compressive (and three-point bend) fracture strain while retaining ≥90 % of the original magnetocaloric and barocaloric figures of merit (|ΔT_ad|, |ΔS_iso|) under the same field (≤2 T) and hydrostatic-pressure (≤100 MPa) cycles near 280–320 K.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted and homogenised single-phase orthorhombic (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 polycrystal, average grain size 50–200 µm, exhibiting ΔT_ad ≈ 3.5 K and |ΔS_iso| ≈ 30 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 2 T / 100 MPa near 300 K but failing by intergranular cracking at <0.5 % compressive strain.
generation.intervention: Add 0.5 at.% elemental boron during the same arc-melting step, followed by identical homogenisation (1000 °C, 24 h, Ar) and water quench.
generation.conditions: Magnetocaloric tests: μ0H = 0–2 T; Barocaloric tests: p = 0–100 MPa; Temperature range 250–350 K; Quasi-static uniaxial compression and three-point bending at 298 K; loading rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron-enriched intergranular films and nanoscale (Fe,Mn)2B borides that pin grain boundaries, reduce average grain size to <10 µm, and increase boundary cohesion.
generation.mechanism: B atoms segregate to grain boundaries during solidification, lowering boundary energy and forming thin boride precipitates that impede crack nucleation and deflect/bridge propagating cracks. Because the B content is <1 %, the parent/final martensitic transformation and the magnetic sub-lattice occupancy remain essentially unchanged, so the first-order magneto-/barocaloric entropy change and transition temperature are only weakly perturbed (≤5 K shift).
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the undoped alloy: (i) room-temperature compressive fracture strain increases from ~0.4 % to ≥0.8 % and compressive strength from ~900 MPa to ≥1.4 GPa; (ii) |ΔT_ad| and |ΔS_iso| at 2 T or 100 MPa decrease by ≤10 % (i.e., remain ≥3.1 K and ≥27 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹); (iii) cyclic fatigue life (10⁴ field/pressure cycles, ±5 K span) at least quadruples before 10 % loss of caloric amplitude.
generation.baseline: Same measurements on the undoped (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy processed identically but without boron.
generation.boundary: Effects expected for total B additions 0.1–1.0 at.% and testing temperatures within ±40 K of the martensitic transition; larger B concentrations or temperatures far from the transition may introduce brittle boride networks or suppress the caloric transition.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: Although B-mediated grain-boundary strengthening is well established in related Fe-based and Ni-Mn-X magnetocaloric alloys, the exact impact on first-order transition sharpness in this quinary HEA has not been directly measured; unanticipated boride coarsening during service could reduce caloric activity.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two 10 g ingots: (A) baseline alloy; (B) same alloy +0.5 at.% B. Apply identical melting, homogenisation, and quench. Cut specimens for (i) room-temperature uniaxial compression, (ii) three-point bending, (iii) direct |ΔT_ad| measurement (IR thermography under 0–2 T field pulses) and (iv) barocaloric calorimetry under 0–100 MPa. Cycle each sample 10⁴ times through the transition by alternating field or pressure at 300 K.
measurements: Compressive yield strength and fracture strain
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if sample B shows (a) <10 % increase in fracture strain OR (b) any decrease ≥15 % in |ΔT_ad| or |ΔS_iso| compared with sample A after identical processing, or (c) caloric fatigue life improvement <2× relative to baseline.
